results.name: ai_search_point_penalty
results.evidence: Computes squared distance from a fetched position (via FUN_0043b2f0) to unaff_EBX+0x28/0x2c/0x30; inside radius unaff_EBX+0x38 it returns a linear falloff (1-dist/radius)*unaff_EBX+0x3c and outputs the distance, otherwise outputs FLT_MAX and returns 0 — a radius/weight proximity cost.
results.summary: Computes a linear-falloff proximity penalty (and outputs the raw distance) of a position relative to a radius/weight record, used as a cost term inside the AI point search.

results.name: ai_search_heap_sift_up
results.evidence: Walks parent index (i-1)>>1 through a short index array at edx+0x1432, compares f-cost floats stored at (node_id+2)*0x28 and swaps entries until heap order holds — classic binary-heap sift-up used by the point-search open list.
results.summary: Sifts a newly pushed open-list entry upward in the AI point search's binary min-heap, ordered by node cost.

results.name: ai_search_heap_sift_down
results.evidence: Standard sift-down: compares children 2i+1/2i+2 costs at (node_id+2)*0x28 in the heap array (ecx+0x1432, count ecx+0x1430) against the root (in_DX) and swaps toward the smaller child.
results.summary: Sifts the heap root down to restore min-heap order in the AI point search's open list after removing the minimum.

results.name: ai_search_open_list_push
results.evidence: Appends a new node (position, source point id param_3, side flag param_4) to the node array at edi+0x30 (stride 0x28), computes edge length via vector2d_normalize_with_length to fill g/f-cost fields, then inserts its index into the heap array (edi+0x1432) and calls the sift-up helper FUN_0043b450.
results.summary: Adds a new open-list node to the AI point-search graph (reusing an existing chained node when appropriate) and pushes it onto the cost-ordered min-heap.

results.name: ai_search_init
results.evidence: Fills a search-context record's header fields from parameters and a start-point lookup via FUN_0043c890, then seeds the open list with the start node by calling FUN_0043b5a0(param_4,param_5,-1,0,0).
results.summary: Initializes an AI point-search context and pushes its initial open-list node.

results.name: ai_search_evaluate_edge
results.evidence: Tests three candidate direct/tangent-offset routes between two points via FUN_0043d790 (navmesh portal check) and compares against a bypass candidate from FUN_0043c8f0, keeping the smallest resulting cost/heading in the output record *param_12.
results.summary: Evaluates the cheapest way (direct or bending around an obstacle) to move between two points for the AI point search, writing the chosen cost and heading.

results.name: ai_search_expand_neighbors
results.evidence: Clears/seeds a visited bitset from param_2 and flood-processes a worklist of point indices, using FUN_0043c9a0 to get an offset target and FUN_0043b830 to score two candidate headings per neighbor before pushing viable ones with FUN_0043b5a0.
results.summary: Breadth-first expands a point's neighbors in the AI navigation point graph, scoring and pushing viable successors onto the open list.

results.name: ai_search_pop_and_expand
results.evidence: Pops the heap minimum via the sift-down helper FUN_0043b4d0, evaluates the popped node's edge cost with FUN_0043b830, and either records a direct connection to the goal via FUN_0043b5a0 or expands the node's neighbors via FUN_0043ba60; returns 1 while the open list still has entries and the goal is unmet.
results.summary: Performs one iteration of the AI point search: pop the cheapest open node and either connect it to the goal or expand its neighbors.

results.name: ai_search_run
results.evidence: Calls FUN_0043b790 to initialize the search, then loops FUN_0043bcb0 until it returns false, reporting success via the goal-found index (+0x1e) or falling back to the best partial node (+0x20).
results.summary: Drives an AI point search to completion, returning whether a full or best-effort path was found.

results.name: ai_pathfind_generate_path
results.evidence: Iterates a waypoint array (param_3, stride 0x10, count param_2), computing per-segment direction/distance, building a local obstacle point graph via FUN_0043c510/FUN_0043cb60, and running the point search machinery to route between successive waypoints; also updates a 'search in progress' counter on the referenced object (param_1[0x12]+0x1058a). Decompilation truncated after ~90 lines.
results.summary: Top-level AI pathfinding entry point that builds an obstacle-aware point graph around a list of waypoints and searches it to produce a full route.

results.name: point_distance_within_radius
results.evidence: Computes 3D squared distance between two point records (in_EAX, in_ECX, fields 0/1/2) and compares against param_1 squared, returning a boolean.
results.summary: Tests whether two 3D points referenced via register operands are within a given radius of each other.

results.name: ray_circle_intersect
results.evidence: Projects the vector from in_ECX to in_EDX onto direction in_EAX; if the projection is non-negative and the perpendicular distance is within radius param_1, computes and writes the near intersection distance via unaff_ESI — a ray/circle intersection test.
results.summary: Ray-versus-circle intersection test used while routing a path around a circular obstacle, returning the entry distance along the ray when it hits.

results.name: circle_tangent_directions
results.evidence: Clamps param_2/param_1 to [-1,1] as a cosine, derives the matching sine, and rotates a base direction vector (in_ECX) by ± that angle to produce two output directions (unaff_ESI, in_EDX) and a projected offset (*param_3) — computing the pair of tangent directions from an offset point to a circle.
results.summary: Computes the two tangent directions from an offset to a circle of a given radius by rotating a base direction vector by the tangent angle in each sense.

results.name: ai_search_obstacle_list_add
results.evidence: Appends a record (id param_1, flag param_2, a vector from unaff_ESI, and param_3) into a fixed 128-entry array at in_EDX+8 (count at in_EDX+2), incrementing a separate 'blocked' counter when bit0 of param_2 is set.
results.summary: Appends a blocker/obstacle record to a capped 128-entry list built while gathering nearby obstacles for the AI point search.

results.name: ai_search_gather_obstacles
results.evidence: Calls object_find_in_sphere to collect nearby objects, filters them by team/state flags, uses object_get_world_matrix and matrix4x3_transform_point on each object's surface points, tests them with point_distance_within_radius (FUN_0043c340), and records qualifying ones via FUN_0043c4b0 — building an obstacle list for a candidate path position.
results.summary: Gathers nearby blocking objects (and their vault/cover surface points) around a candidate search position into the obstacle list used by the AI point search.

results.name: ai_search_find_point_covering
results.evidence: Scans the fixed point array (unaff_ESI, stride 0x14, count at +2), skipping unaff_BX, and returns the first index whose own radius (offset+0x10) plus param_1 reaches the position at in_EDX.
results.summary: Finds a point in the search's fixed point array whose coverage radius reaches a given position, or -1 if none does.

results.name: ai_search_find_nearest_point
results.evidence: Scans the point array (param_1, stride 0x14, count at +2), skipping param_2 and optionally flagged (bit0) entries when param_7 is set, filters via ray_circle_intersect (FUN_0043c380), and keeps the closest match by running distance, writing the best distance/point id to unaff_EDI.
results.summary: Finds the closest point in the point array visible along a given direction, optionally excluding flagged points, returning its distance and id.

results.name: ai_search_point_tangent_offset
results.evidence: Computes the normalized direction/distance from a point-array entry (in_ECX+8+in_AX*0x14) to *in_EDX and calls circle_tangent_directions (FUN_0043c400) using the point's own radius (+0.00390625 slack) to derive steer-around offsets.
results.summary: Computes tangent offset directions for steering around a specific point-array entry, used while scoring candidate path edges.

results.name: ai_search_flood_fill_reachable
results.evidence: Clears a bitset sized to the point array's count, seeds it with the start index in_DX, and BFS-expands to any other point whose combined radii cover the distance between them, marking all reached indices in the bitset.
results.summary: Flood-fills the set of point-graph indices reachable from a starting point through pairwise proximity links.

results.name: ai_search_assign_point_groups
results.evidence: For every point still ungrouped (group field at [idx*10+5] == -1), allocates a new group id (unaff_ESI[0]++) and flood-fills its connected set via FUN_0043ca40, tagging every reached index with that group id — computing connected components of the point graph.
results.summary: Partitions the point graph into connected groups by repeatedly flood-filling from each ungrouped point.

results.name: ai_navmesh_simplify_path
results.evidence: Iterates a source path (param_3, stride 0x10, count param_2), extending a clear line-of-sight run as far as possible using FUN_0043de90, then computing the exact shortcut corner via FUN_0043d4b0/FUN_0043d240 and appending compressed waypoints to param_5 (capped at 4 output points) — a string-pulling path simplification pass. Decompilation truncated at the end (3 lines).
results.summary: Simplifies a raw waypoint path into a small set of shortcut points by greedily extending clear segments and snapping to occluding navmesh corners.

results.name: ai_navmesh_circle_segment_intersect
results.evidence: Solves the quadratic for where a circle of radius param_1 centered on in_ECX intersects relative to in_EDX, then selects one of the two tangent solutions based on which side (via a cross-product sign test against param_2) is requested.
results.summary: Finds the tangent point where a path must bend around a circular navmesh obstacle vertex, on the requested side.

results.name: ai_navmesh_portal_edge_intersect
results.evidence: Computes where a circle of radius param_1 intersects the line through in_ECX/in_EDX (a portal edge), validating the result is close to the edge midpoint, and otherwise falls back to a normalized offset from unaff_EDI along the edge direction.
results.summary: Computes where a given-radius circle crosses a portal edge, falling back to a direction-based offset if the edge geometry is degenerate.

results.name: ai_navmesh_choose_shorter_corner
results.evidence: Computes four turn angles via vector2d_angle_between and selects between two candidate corner points (param_1 vs unaff_EBX) based on which combination sums to a smaller turn, writing the chosen corner into *param_3.
results.summary: Chooses whichever of two candidate polygon corners produces the shorter combined turn when a path bends around an obstacle.

results.name: ai_navmesh_trace_cluster_boundary
results.evidence: Walks a BSP cluster's edge table (iVar3+0x4c, stride 0x18) from vertex in_EAX, testing each edge's permission bit (with a team-indexed bit-array override) against a proposed move direction (param_1,param_2), returning the boundary vertex/edge where the move first exits the cluster.
results.summary: Walks a BSP cluster's boundary edges to find where a proposed straight-line move first crosses a blocked or permission boundary.

results.name: ai_navmesh_raycast_cluster_edges
results.evidence: Repeatedly calls FUN_005017f0 to step across a cluster's edge list from a starting vertex, testing candidate edge distances against param_5 and each edge's passable flag (with a team-indexed bit-array override), returning the nearest blocking edge's distance/normal in param_6.
results.summary: Traces along a cluster's boundary edges from a starting vertex, returning the nearest edge that would block a proposed move within range.

results.name: ai_navmesh_same_cluster_height
results.evidence: Fetches height values for two cluster/vertex indices via FUN_0044d860 and returns whether they differ by less than 0.05 units.
results.summary: Checks whether two navmesh cluster locations sit at nearly the same height, used to reject path steps needing a large vertical jump.

results.name: ai_navmesh_find_crossing_portal
results.evidence: Recursively calls itself (FUN_0043d9b0) while walking a cluster's connected edges from param_4 toward the segment param_3->param_5, checking each edge's orientation and a team-indexed permission bit array (DAT_0069e8d8/DAT_006b8d78), and reports via param_7 the first portal/edge the segment crosses. Decompilation truncated (18 lines).
results.summary: Recursively traces a straight segment across a BSP cluster's connected edges to find the first portal boundary it crosses.

results.name: ai_navmesh_line_of_sight_clear
results.evidence: Early-outs for coincident endpoints; otherwise calls FUN_0043d9b0 from each endpoint's cluster to find the nearest crossing boundary, compares the two results, and if a crossing lies within param_5 of one endpoint copies its portal/edge data to param_7 as the blocking result.
results.summary: Determines whether a straight segment between two points is unobstructed across BSP cluster portals within a margin, reporting the first blocking crossing if any.

results.name: actor_firing_position_acquire
results.evidence: Walks an actor's (param_1) linked list of firing-position nodes (DAT_00880360 array, stride 0x724, node pool DAT_008802c0 stride 0x138) looking for a reusable node of type param_3 or the best-scoring free candidate; calls datum_new when none qualifies, then re-links it via actor_replace_object_reference/FUN_0043ea20 and reinitializes it via FUN_0043e640.
results.summary: Finds or allocates a per-actor firing-position node of the requested type, reinitializing it when newly allocated or repurposed.

results.name: actor_firing_position_node_init
results.evidence: Initializes a (re)acquired node's fields from its referenced object's cluster data (cluster index at +0x12, flags from FUN_0045bd50/FUN_0045bdb0/FUN_0045be00, a cover flag copied from the object record, and a 1000-unit timer when covered), then links the node onto that object's per-cluster list head at DAT_00880360[...]+0x50.
results.summary: Initializes a firing-position node's fields from its target object (cluster, cover flags, timers) and links it into that object's node list.

results.name: actor_firing_position_node_copy
results.evidence: Bulk-copies a 0x138-byte node record (0x4e dwords) from puVar8 to puVar6 while preserving header fields, resets several timer/flag fields, recomputes an offset vector from two stored points, and copies a constant vector from PTR_DAT_00696714.
results.summary: Copies a firing-position node record into another slot and resets its per-instance runtime state.

results.name: actor_firing_position_node_new
results.evidence: Allocates a node via datum_new, initializes it with FUN_0043e640, then on success links it as the counterpart of param_2 via actor_firing_position_node_copy (FUN_0043e840) and cross-referenced index fields at offset 0xc.
results.summary: Allocates a new firing-position node and links it as the paired counterpart of an existing node.

results.name: actor_firing_position_node_new_typed
results.evidence: Same allocate/init/link pattern as FUN_0043e910, additionally copying a bounded type value (in [4,6)) from param_3's node field +0x24 onto the newly created node.
results.summary: Allocates and links a new firing-position node as the counterpart of an existing one, propagating a bounded type value from a third reference node.

results.name: actor_firing_position_node_unlink
results.evidence: Walks the singly-linked node list rooted at DAT_00880360[...]+0x50 for the current object (in_EAX), chaining through each node's +8 next field, and removes the entry matching unaff_EDI.
results.summary: Removes a firing-position node from its owning object's linked list of nodes.

results.name: actor_firing_position_find_matching
results.evidence: Walks an object's (in_ECX) firing-position node list skipping types in [0,2), matching a node whose owner field equals param_1 or whose cluster field (offset+0x1c) equals the target object's cluster (looked up via DAT_008603b0).
results.summary: Searches an object's firing-position node list for one owned by a given actor or matching a target's cluster, skipping reserved node types.

results.name: actor_get_or_create_firing_position
results.evidence: Looks up an existing shared firing-position node between actor param_1 and target in_EAX via a list walk, or (when param_2 is set and the target allows it) creates one with actor_firing_position_acquire (FUN_0043e270); configures it via FUN_0041c4b0/FUN_0041c8f0 and, for wide targets (field +0x30 > 1), resets combat flags via actor_target_reset_combat_flags.
results.summary: Finds or creates a shared firing-position node between an actor and a target object and initializes its combat-relevant fields.

results.name: actor_firing_position_list_head
results.evidence: Writes the current object's (in_EAX) firing-position list head index (DAT_00880360[...]+0x50) into *param_1 — a one-line accessor.
results.summary: Returns the head index of the current object's firing-position node linked list.

results.name: actor_firing_position_list_iterator_next
results.evidence: Classic {current,next} iterator step: copies in_EDX[1] into *in_EDX, then if that id is valid fetches the node's own next field (+8) into in_EDX[1] for the following call, returning the current node's record offset.
results.summary: Advances a {current,next} iterator over the firing-position node linked list, returning the current node's record offset.
